citation: [John J. Glessner], The Commercial Club of Chicago: Its Beginning and Something of Its Work (Chicago: privately printed for presentation to members of the Commercial Club, Binner-Wells Company, printers, 1910), p. 81, plate 'Former Presidents of the Commercial Club': the halftone portrait captioned 'John J. Glessner 1897'.
author: John J. Glessner
repository: Library of Congress copy, digitised by the Internet Archive, item commercialclubof00gles.
locator: p. 81 (scan leaf 95), lower left of four portraits; the caption gives the year of his presidency of the club (1897), not the year the photograph was taken.
rights_note: A book printed in the United States in 1910, in the public domain; the Library of Congress states it is unaware of any copyright restrictions on the item.
access_notes: Found 2026-11-06 (T-3413) through the Internet Archive record of the book, which the Library of Congress catalogues under Glessner; the plate was read at the scan's 3000-pixel page image (leaf95_w3000.jpg).
note: A head-and-shoulders photograph of Glessner turned about a quarter towards his left, in round wire spectacles, a full grey moustache, a dark coat and tie with a wing collar; the crown of his head is bald with white hair at the sides. The photograph is undated: he was 67 when the book was printed.
what_it_supplies: the proportions of Glessner's face (eyes, nose, mouth, chin and ear) as one photograph shows them
that he wore spectacles and a moustache in the photograph
what_it_does_not_supply: the date the photograph was taken
his face's depth (one view only), its colour, or his height and build below the shoulders
